prs.title: Lazy member resolution for class and interface types
prs.author: ahejlsberg
prs.body:
Inspired by #64765, this PR implements lazy member resolution for class and interface types. The PR computes shared member layouts for classes and interfaces and uses these layouts to lazily populate the properties of type instances.

The single baseline change is due to an improvement in member sorting that causes the numerically named members and the `length` member of tuple types to be sorted before those members that are inherited from `Array<T>`.

prs.title: Don't resolve mapped type members to find their signatures
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Mapped types never have call or construct signatures, but asking for their signatures resolved all of their properties. Signature checks in relations ask for them first, so every mapped type that reached a relation had its properties built, even when nothing else needed them. In MUI, components accept `Partial<...>` of each intrinsic element's props, so this built hundreds of properties for each of thousands of such types, and their combined base properties too.

Measured with --checkers 4 (n=6):

```
                      │  old.txt   │             new.txt              │
                      │   sec/op   │   sec/op    vs base              │
    Tsc/bluesky         2.459 ± 3%   2.458 ± 3%       ~ (p=0.818 n=6)
    Tsc/sentry          10.21 ± 4%   10.27 ± 3%       ~ (p=0.937 n=6)
    Tsc/t3code-server   8.097 ± 3%   8.085 ± 1%       ~ (p=0.937 n=6)
    Tsc/mui-docs        6.423 ± 4%   5.902 ± 4%  -8.10% (p=0.002 n=6)
    geomean             6.011        5.892       -1.98%

                      │   old.txt    │              new.txt               │
                      │    rss-B     │    rss-B      vs base              │
    Tsc/bluesky         1.184Gi ± 1%   1.176Gi ± 3%       ~ (p=0.699 n=6)
    Tsc/sentry          3.415Gi ± 5%   3.273Gi ± 5%       ~ (p=0.240 n=6)
    Tsc/t3code-server   2.875Gi ± 6%   2.913Gi ± 8%       ~ (p=0.699 n=6)
    Tsc/mui-docs        2.323Gi ± 7%   2.203Gi ± 5%       ~ (p=0.240 n=6)
    geomean             2.280Gi        2.229Gi       -2.21%
